sentences.zh: 志三十 地理二 奉天 ：禹貢青、冀二州之域。

translations.literal: Geography 2, Fengtian: Within the territory of the Qing and Ji prefectures in the Yugong.
translations.idiomatic: Geography 2, Fengtian: The region corresponded to the Qing and Ji prefectures in the Tribute of Yu.

sentences.zh: （舜析其東北為幽、營。

translations.literal: (Shun divided off its northeast as You and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: (In Shun's time its northeast was set apart as the You and Ying regions.

sentences.zh: 夏仍青、冀。

translations.literal: Under Xia it remained Qing and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Xia it was still counted as Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: 商改營州。

translations.literal: Under Shang it was changed to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Shang it was reorganized as Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 周，幽州。

translations.literal: Under Zhou, Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou it was Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 明，遼東都指揮使司。）

translations.idiomatic: In the Ming it was the Liaodong Regional Military Commission.)

sentences.zh: 清天命十年三月，定都瀋陽。

translations.literal: In the third month of the tenth year of Tianming of Qing, the capital was fixed at Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the tenth year of the Qing Tianming era, the capital was established at Shenyang.

sentences.zh: 天聦八年，尊為盛京。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tiancong, it was honored as Shengjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Tiancong it was elevated to the title Shengjing.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，悉裁明諸衞所，設內大臣、副都統，及八旗駐防。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, all Ming guards and posts were abolished, and inner ministers, lieutenant-generals, and Eight Banner garrisons were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Shunzhi year the Ming guard and post system was abolished entirely; inner ministers, lieutenant-generals, and Eight Banner garrisons were put in place.

sentences.zh: 三年，改內大臣為昂邦章京，給鎮守總管印。

translations.literal: In the third year, inner ministers were changed to ambanaggi, and seals of garrison commander were conferred.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later the inner ministers were retitled ambanaggi and given seals as territorial garrison commanders.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，改昂邦章京為鎮守遼東等處地方將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, ambanaggi were changed to Generals for Garrisoning Liaodong and Other Places.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 1 the ambanaggi became the General for Garrisoning Liaodong and Vicinity.

sentences.zh: 四年，改鎮守奉天等處地方將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, changed to General for Garrisoning Fengtian and Other Places.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the title became General for Garrisoning Fengtian and Vicinity.

sentences.zh: 光緒三十三年三月，罷將軍，置東三省總督、奉天巡撫，改為行省。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirty-third year of Guangxu, the general was abolished, the Three Eastern Provinces governor-general and Fengtian governor were established, and it was changed to a regular province.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Guangxu 33 the generalship was abolished; a governor-general of the Three Eastern Provinces and a Fengtian governor were appointed, and Fengtian was converted to a conventional provincial administration.

sentences.zh: 北至洮南；

translations.literal: On the north it reached to Taonan;
translations.idiomatic: Its northern boundary ran to Taonan;

translations.literal: (bordering Heilongjiang.)
translations.idiomatic: (where it bordered Heilongjiang.)

sentences.zh: 南至旅順口；

translations.literal: On the south to Lüshunkou;
translations.idiomatic: On the south to Lüshunkou;

sentences.zh: （海界東南，以鴨綠江與朝鮮界。）

translations.literal: (On the southeast the sea border, with Korea bounded by the Yalu River.)
translations.idiomatic: (Along the southeastern coast it met Korea across the Yalu River.)

sentences.zh: 西至山海關；

translations.literal: On the west to Shanhaiguan;
translations.idiomatic: On the west to Shanhaiguan;

sentences.zh: （與直隸界。）

translations.literal: (bordering Zhili.)
translations.idiomatic: (where it bordered Zhili.)

sentences.zh: 東至安圖。

translations.literal: On the east to Antu.
translations.idiomatic: On the east to Antu.

sentences.zh: （與吉林界。）

translations.literal: (bordering Jilin.)
translations.idiomatic: (Bordering Jilin.)

sentences.zh: 廣一千八百里，袤一千七百五十里。

translations.literal: Its breadth was one thousand eight hundred li, its length one thousand seven hundred fifty li.
translations.idiomatic: It measured one thousand eight hundred li from east to west and one thousand seven hundred fifty li from north to south.

sentences.zh: 北極高三十九度四十分至四十四度十五分。

translations.literal: North polar altitude from thirty-nine degrees forty minutes to forty-four degrees fifteen minutes.
translations.idiomatic: Its latitude ranged from 39°40′ to 44°15′ north.

sentences.zh: 京師偏東四度至十二度。

translations.literal: East of the capital by four to twelve degrees.
translations.idiomatic: It lay four to twelve degrees east of the capital.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年，編戶一百六十五萬五百七十三，口一千六十九萬六千零四。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuantong, registered households numbered 1,650,573 and population 10,696,004.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 3 there were 1,650,573 registered households and a population of 10,696,004.

sentences.zh: 共領府八，直隸廳五，廳三，州六，縣三十三。

translations.literal: In all it administered eight prefectures, five directly subordinate departments, three departments, six subprefectures, and thirty-three counties.
translations.idiomatic: In all it comprised eight prefectures, five departments under direct provincial control, three departments, six subprefectures, and thirty-three counties.

sentences.zh: （案：盛京，天聦五年因明瀋陽衞城增修。

translations.literal: (Note: Shengjing, in the fifth year of Tiancong was enlarged and repaired on the basis of the Ming Shenyang guard city.
translations.idiomatic: (Note: Shengjing was enlarged and rebuilt in Tiancong 5 on the site of the Ming Shenyang guard city.

sentences.zh: 城周九里三百三十二步，高三丈五尺，厚一丈，女牆高七尺五寸，垛口凡六百五十一。

translations.literal: The city wall circuited nine li three hundred thirty-two paces, was three zhang five chi high, one zhang thick, the parapet seven chi five cun high, and battlements numbered six hundred fifty-one in all.
translations.idiomatic: The wall ran nine li and 332 paces around the city, stood 3 zhang 5 chi high and 1 zhang thick, with a parapet 7 chi 5 cun high and 651 crenellations in all.

sentences.zh: 門八：東之左曰撫近，右曰內治，南之左曰德盛，右曰天祐，西之左曰懷遠，右曰外攘，北之左曰地載，右曰福勝。

translations.literal: There were eight gates: on the east, left called Fujin, right called Neizhi; on the south, left called Desheng, right called Tianyou; on the west, left called Huaiyuan, right called Wairang; on the north, left called Dizai, right called Fusheng.
translations.idiomatic: There were eight gates: on the east, the left was Fujin and the right Neizhi; on the south, the left Desheng and the right Tianyou; on the west, the left Huaiyuan and the right Wairang; on the north, the left Dizai and the right Fusheng.

sentences.zh: 門各有樓闉，加之角樓。

translations.literal: Each gate had a barbican tower, with corner towers added.
translations.idiomatic: Each gate had a barbican tower, and corner towers were added as well.

sentences.zh: 四城之中為大政殿，太宗聽政之所也。

translations.literal: Within the four-walled city was the Grand Politics Hall, where Taizong heard government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the center of the inner city stood the Grand Politics Hall, where Taizong held court.

sentences.zh: 殿西為大內。

translations.literal: West of the hall was the Great Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: West of the hall lay the Great Inner Palace.

sentences.zh: 南向曰大清門，門內曰崇政殿，殿前東飛龍閣，西翔鳳閣。

translations.literal: Facing south was the Daqing Gate; within the gate was the Chongzheng Hall; before the hall east was the Feilong Pavilion, west the Xiangfeng Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Facing south was the Daqing Gate; inside it stood Chongzheng Hall, with Feilong Pavilion to the east and Xiangfeng Pavilion to the west before the hall.

sentences.zh: 崇政殿直北為鳳凰樓，樓北清寧宮。

translations.literal: Directly north of Chongzheng Hall was Fenghuang Tower; north of the tower, Qingning Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Directly north of Chongzheng Hall stood Fenghuang Tower, and north of the tower lay Qingning Palace.

sentences.zh: 宮之東曰衍慶宮、關睢宮，西曰永福宮、麟趾宮。

translations.literal: East of the palace were Yanqing Palace and Guansui Palace; west were Yongfu Palace and Linzhi Palace.
translations.idiomatic: East of the palace were Yanqing and Guansui palaces; to the west were Yongfu and Linzhi palaces.

sentences.zh: 鳳凰樓之前，東為師善齋，齋南日華樓，西協中齋，齋南霞綺樓。

translations.literal: Before Fenghuang Tower, east was Shishan Studio, south of the studio Rihua Tower; west Xiezhong Studio, south of the studio Xiaqi Tower.
translations.idiomatic: Before Fenghuang Tower, to the east was Shishan Studio with Rihua Tower south of it; to the west was Xiezhong Studio with Xiaqi Tower south of it.

sentences.zh: 崇政殿東頤和殿，殿後介祉宮，宮後為敬典閣。

translations.literal: East of Chongzheng Hall was Yihe Hall; behind the hall Jiezhi Palace; behind the palace Jingdian Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: East of Chongzheng Hall stood Yihe Hall; behind the hall was Jiezhi Palace, and behind the palace Jingdian Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 崇政殿西為迪光殿，殿後保極宮，宮後繼思齋，齋後崇謨閣。

translations.literal: West of Chongzheng Hall was Diguang Hall; behind the hall Baoji Palace; behind the palace Jisi Studio; behind the studio Chongmo Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: West of Chongzheng Hall stood Diguang Hall; behind the hall was Baoji Palace, behind the palace Jisi Studio, and behind the studio Chongmo Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 大內之西文溯閣，藏書之所也。

translations.literal: West of the Great Inner Palace was Wensu Pavilion, a place for storing books.
translations.idiomatic: West of the Great Inner Palace stood Wensu Pavilion, the book depository.

sentences.zh: 東南太廟。

translations.literal: Southeast was the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast lay the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 銀庫在大政殿南，織造庫在大內南。

translations.literal: The silver treasury was south of the Grand Politics Hall; the weaving depot south of the Great Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The silver treasury stood south of the Grand Politics Hall, and the weaving depot south of the Great Inner Palace.

sentences.zh: 戶部、禮部、工部在銀庫東，刑部、兵部在織造庫西。

translations.literal: The Boards of Revenue, Rites, and Works were east of the silver treasury; the Boards of Punishments and War west of the weaving depot.
translations.idiomatic: The Boards of Revenue, Rites, and Works lay east of the silver treasury; the Boards of Punishments and War west of the weaving depot.

sentences.zh: 御史公署在城東北隅。

translations.literal: The censorate office was in the northeast corner of the city.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate office stood in the city's northeast corner.

sentences.zh: 其外關城則康熙十九年建，高七尺五寸，周三十二里四十八步。

translations.literal: The outer barrier city was built in the nineteenth year of Kangxi, seven chi five cun high, circuiting thirty-two li forty-eight paces.
translations.idiomatic: The outer barrier city was built in Kangxi 19; it was 7 chi 5 cun high and ran thirty-two li and 48 paces around.

sentences.zh: 門八：東之左曰小東關，右曰大東關，南之左曰大南關，右曰小南關，西之左曰大西關，右曰小西關，北之左曰小北關，右曰大北關。

translations.literal: There were eight gates: on the east, left called Xiaodong Pass, right called Dadong Pass; on the south, left called Danan Pass, right called Xiaonan Pass; on the west, left called Daxi Pass, right called Xiaoxi Pass; on the north, left called Xiaobei Pass, right called Dabei Pass.
translations.idiomatic: It had eight gates: on the east, the left Xiaodong Pass and the right Dadong Pass; on the south, the left Danan Pass and the right Xiaonan Pass; on the west, the left Daxi Pass and the right Xiaoxi Pass; on the north, the left Xiaobei Pass and the right Dabei Pass.

sentences.zh: 關城內南為天壇，東為地壇、為堂子，西南隅為社稷壇、為雷雨壇，東南隅為先農祠、為耤田。

translations.literal: Within the barrier city, south was the Altar of Heaven; east the Altar of Earth and the Tangzi; southwest corner the Altars of Soil and Grain and of Thunder and Rain; southeast corner the Shrine of the First Farmer and the sacred plough field.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the barrier city the Altar of Heaven stood to the south; to the east were the Altar of Earth and the Tangzi; in the southwest corner were the Altars of Soil and Grain and of Thunder and Rain; in the southeast corner were the Shrine of the First Farmer and the sacred plough field.

sentences.zh: 耤田西南隅設水門二，導小瀋水自門出焉，下流注於渾河。

translations.literal: At the southwest corner of the sacred plough field two sluice gates were set, conducting the Lesser Shen River out through the gates; downstream it entered the Hun River.
translations.idiomatic: Two sluice gates at the southwest corner of the sacred plough field channeled the Lesser Shen River outward; downstream it flowed into the Hun River.

sentences.zh: 其名山為醫巫閭、松嶺。

translations.literal: Its famous mountains were Yiwulü and Songling.
translations.idiomatic: Its notable mountains were Yiwulü and Songling.

sentences.zh: 其巨川為遼河、渾河。

translations.literal: Its great rivers were the Liao River and the Hun River.
translations.idiomatic: Its major rivers were the Liao and the Hun.

sentences.zh: 其重險：山海關、鳳凰城、威遠堡。

translations.literal: Its major strategic points: Shanhaiguan, Fenghuang City, and Weiyuan Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Its chief strategic points were Shanhaiguan, Fenghuang City, and Weiyuan Fort.

sentences.zh: 其船路：自營口西南通天津，南通之罘，東南通朝鮮仁川。

translations.literal: Its shipping routes: from Yingkou southwest to Tianjin, south to Zhifu, southeast to Inchon in Korea.
translations.idiomatic: Its shipping routes ran from Yingkou southwest to Tianjin, south to Zhifu, and southeast to Inchon in Korea.

sentences.zh: 其鐵路：內屬者，營榆；

translations.literal: Its railways: domestically controlled, Ying-Yu;
translations.idiomatic: Its railways included the domestically controlled Ying-Yu line;

sentences.zh: 屬日者，俄築東清枝路。

translations.literal: under Japanese control, the Russian-built Eastern Qing branch line.
translations.idiomatic: under Japanese control, the Russian-built Eastern Qing branch line.

sentences.zh: 其電線：西通天津，西南旅順，東南鳳凰、安東，東北吉林。）：

translations.literal: Its telegraph lines: west to Tianjin, southwest to Lüshun, southeast to Fenghuang and Andong, northeast to Jilin.):
translations.idiomatic: Telegraph lines ran west to Tianjin, southwest to Lüshun, southeast to Fenghuang and Andong, and northeast to Jilin.):

translations.literal: The governor-general also held the generalship; civil affairs, judicial, foreign affairs, and finance commissioners, the salt transport intendant, the industrial promotion circuit intendant, and a lieutenant-general were stationed there.)
translations.idiomatic: The governor-general doubled as general; commissioners for civil affairs, judicial affairs, foreign affairs, and finance, the salt transport intendant, the industrial promotion circuit intendant, and a lieutenant-general were stationed there.)

sentences.zh: 順治十四年四月，於盛京城內置府，設府尹。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourteenth year of Shunzhi, a prefecture was established within Shengjing city and a prefectural intendant was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Shunzhi 14 a prefecture was established within Shengjing city with a prefectural intendant.

sentences.zh: 光緒三十一年八月，裁府尹設知府，為奉天省治。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the thirty-first year of Guangxu, the prefectural intendant was abolished and a prefect was established as the provincial seat of Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Guangxu 31 the prefectural intendant was abolished and a prefect appointed, making the city the seat of Fengtian province.

sentences.zh: 西南至京師一千四百七十里。

translations.literal: Southwest to the capital one thousand four hundred seventy li.
translations.idiomatic: It lay one thousand four hundred seventy li southwest of the capital.

sentences.zh: 廣八百七十里，袤九百九十里。

translations.literal: Breadth eight hundred seventy li, length nine hundred ninety li.
translations.idiomatic: It measured eight hundred seventy li from east to west and nine hundred ninety li from north to south.

sentences.zh: 北極高四十一度五十一分五十秒。

translations.literal: North polar altitude forty-one degrees fifty-one minutes fifty seconds.
translations.idiomatic: Its latitude was 41°51′50″ north.

sentences.zh: 京師偏東七度十五分。

translations.literal: East of the capital by seven degrees fifteen minutes.
translations.idiomatic: It lay seven degrees fifteen minutes east of the capital.

sentences.zh: 領廳一，州二，縣八。

translations.literal: It administered one department, two subprefectures, and eight counties.
translations.idiomatic: It comprised one department, two subprefectures, and eight counties.

sentences.zh: 承德：（衝，繁，疲，難。

translations.literal: Chengde: (Chong, fan, pi, nan.
translations.idiomatic: Chengde: (Rated chong, fan, pi, and nan.

sentences.zh: 倚。

translations.literal: Attached.
translations.idiomatic: Attached to the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 明，瀋陽中衞。

translations.literal: Under Ming, Shenyang Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the Ming it was Shenyang Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年置縣，附府。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kangxi a county was established, attached to the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A county was established in Kangxi 3 and attached to the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 福陵在東二十里天柱山，昭陵在西北十里隆業山。

translations.literal: Fuling was twenty li east on Tianzhu Mountain; Zhaoling ten li northwest on Longye Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Fuling lay twenty li east on Tianzhu Mountain; Zhaoling ten li northwest on Longye Mountain.

sentences.zh: 有副都統兼二陵守衞大臣。

translations.literal: There was a lieutenant-general who also served as guardian minister of the two mausoleums.
translations.idiomatic: A lieutenant-general also served as guardian minister of the two imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 渾河在南，卽瀋水，自撫順入，西南入遼中。

translations.literal: The Hun River was on the south, that is the Shen River; it entered from Fushun and went southwest into Liaozhong.
translations.idiomatic: The Hun River lay to the south; it was the Shen River, entering from Fushun and flowing southwest into Liaozhong.

sentences.zh: 左受高素屯、白塔鋪、於家臺河，右受馬官橋、萬泉河。

translations.literal: On the left it received the Gaosutun, Baitapu, and Yujiatai rivers; on the right the Maguanqiao and Wanquan rivers.
translations.idiomatic: From the left it received the Gaosutun, Baitapu, and Yujiatai rivers; from the right the Maguanqiao and Wanquan rivers.

sentences.zh: 萬泉亦稱小瀋水。

translations.literal: Wanquan was also called the Lesser Shen River.
translations.idiomatic: The Wanquan was also known as the Lesser Shen River.

sentences.zh: 東北：大清山，蒲河所出，西南流，逕永安橋，入新民境。

translations.literal: Northeast: Daqing Mountain, whence the Pu River issued; it flowed southwest, passed Yong'an Bridge, and entered Xinmin territory.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast stood Daqing Mountain, source of the Pu River, which flowed southwest past Yong'an Bridge into Xinmin.

sentences.zh: 永安橋，崇德六年建。

translations.literal: Yong'an Bridge was built in the sixth year of Chongde.
translations.idiomatic: Yong'an Bridge was built in Chongde 6.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖定瀋陽，以西路沮洳，命旗丁修疊道百二十里，直抵遼陽。

translations.literal: At first, when Taizu fixed Shenyang, because the western route was marshy, he ordered banner soldiers to build a raised road one hundred twenty li, running straight to Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu first established Shenyang, the western route was so marshy that he ordered banner troops to build a raised road one hundred twenty li long straight to Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 太宗復建此橋，行旅便之。

translations.literal: Taizong rebuilt this bridge, to the convenience of travelers.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong rebuilt this bridge, which greatly eased travel.

sentences.zh: 舊設驛四：西老邊，通新民；

translations.literal: Formerly four courier stations were established: Laobian in the west, connecting to Xinmin;
translations.idiomatic: Four courier stations had formerly been established: Laobian in the west, linking Xinmin;

sentences.zh: 北懿路，通鐵嶺；

translations.literal: Yilu in the north, connecting to Tieling;
translations.idiomatic: Yilu in the north, linking Tieling;

sentences.zh: 東噶布拉村，通興京；

translations.literal: Gabulacun in the east, connecting to Xingjing;
translations.idiomatic: Gabulacun in the east, linking Xingjing;

sentences.zh: 南十里河，卽明虎皮驛，通遼陽。

translations.literal: Shilihe in the south, that is the Ming Hupi courier station, connecting to Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shilihe in the south, the Ming Hupi courier station, linking Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 鐵路三：京奉，東清，安奉。

translations.literal: Three railways: Jing-Feng, Eastern Qing, and An-Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Three railways served the area: the Jing-Feng, Eastern Qing, and An-Feng lines.

sentences.zh: 京奉鐵路行境內六十里，車站二，曰馬三家，曰瀋陽，在小西關外，卽京奉全路尾站。

translations.literal: The Jing-Feng Railway ran sixty li within the territory; there were two stations, called Masanjia and Shenyang; the latter was outside Xiaoxi Pass, the terminus of the entire Jing-Feng line.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing-Feng Railway ran sixty li within the county, with two stations, Masanjia and Shenyang; the latter stood outside Xiaoxi Pass and was the terminus of the entire Jing-Feng line.

sentences.zh: 商埠，光緒二十九年八月中美約開。）

translations.literal: A commercial port, opened in the eighth month of the twenty-ninth year of Guangxu by Sino-American treaty.)
translations.idiomatic: A treaty port was opened in the eighth month of Guangxu 29 under the Sino-American agreement.)

sentences.zh: 遼陽州：（繁，疲，難。

translations.literal: Liaoyang Subprefecture: (Fan, pi, nan.
